methods.name: LOFT
methods.full_name: Low-Rank Orthogonal Fine-Tuning via Task-Aware Support Selection
methods.paper_title: LOFT: Low-Rank Orthogonal Fine-Tuning via Task-Aware Support Selection
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0\,S(P_r,T_r),\quad S(P_r,T_r)=I_{d_{in}}+P_r^{\top}(T_r-I_r)P_r,\quad P_r\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},\ P_rP_r^{\top}=I_r\ \text{(support, frozen)},\quad T_r=Q(E)\in SO(r),\ E\in\mathrm{Skew}(r)\ \text{(trained, }E_0=0;\ \text{paper: Cayley; released code: 5-term Cayley--Neumann)};\quad \text{supports: } P_r=V_r^{\top}\ \text{(principal)},\ \text{top right singular subspace of } G=\nabla_W L(W_0)\ \text{(GradSVD)},\ \text{top invariant subspace of } \operatorname{skew}(W_0^{\top}G)\ \text{(SkewGrad)}
methods.locus: any linear layer; acts on the input side (right multiplication of \(W_0\))
methods.structure: Right action of \(SO(V)\), the rotations of the chosen \(r\)-dimensional input subspace \(V=\operatorname{row}P_r\) that fix \(V^{\perp}\) pointwise (exactly orthogonal only with an exact \(Q\); the code's Cayley–Neumann default is approximate). The induced additive update \(\Delta W=W_0P_r^{\top}(T_r-I_r)P_r\) has rank at most \(r\). The paper's multi-factor primitive \(W_0\prod_{\ell}S(P^{(\ell)}_{r_\ell},T^{(\ell)}_{r_\ell})\), with general transforms and, for HRA, learnable width-one supports, recovers full and block OFT, GOFT, BOFT and HRA, and PSOFT up to its two scaling vectors.
methods.mergeable_reason: \(W_0S(P_r,T_r)\) is again a weight matrix, equal to \(W_0+W_0P_r^{\top}(T_r-I_r)P_r\).
methods.identity_at_init: \(E=0\) gives \(T_r=I_r\) and \(S=I\), so the model is unchanged. The support \(P_r\) is computed once before training: from the SVD of \(W_0\) (principal), or from the gradient \(G\) of the downstream loss at \(W_0\) estimated on a small calibration set (GradSVD, SkewGrad), then frozen.
methods.key_idea: Separate where an orthogonal update acts (the support \(P_r\)) from how it acts (the in-subspace transform \(T_r\)), and choose the support from the task: the first-order training signal of a right-subspace rotation is \(P_r\operatorname{skew}(W_0^{\top}G)P_r^{\top}\), whose norm is largest when \(P_r\) spans the top invariant subspace of \(\operatorname{skew}(W_0^{\top}G)\).
methods.results_note: With SkewGrad support at \(r=46\), the GLUE average on DeBERTaV3-base is 88.73 against 88.04 for PSOFT, and the VTAB-1K average on ViT-B/16 is 73.8 against 73.4, with 0.07M trainable parameters; principal-support LOFT matches PSOFT (88.06).

relations.note: Principal-support LOFT is PSOFT with both scaling vectors frozen at 1, when both use the same exactly orthogonal transform.
HRA is an instance of the paper's multi-factor primitive with learnable width-one supports, not of fixed-support LOFT; LOFT's image is one leaf of HRA's image.
Block OFT is an instance of the paper's multi-factor primitive with coordinate-block supports; single-factor LOFT maps into full-block exact-Cayley OFT.
GOFT is a depth-L composition of width-2 coordinate-pair supports in the paper's multi-factor primitive.
BOFT is a multi-stage composition of butterfly-block supports in the paper's multi-factor primitive.
Both choose a starting frame from the gradient at W_0: LoRA-GA for an additive low-rank update, LOFT (GradSVD, SkewGrad) for an orthogonal support.

methods.verification_notes: Added 2026-10-02 after a reader reported it missing. Title, authors and date checked against the arXiv API; formula, supports, parameter count and results read from the paper (Sections 2-3, Tables 1-4, Appendix C.1). Two independent referees checked the entry and the site text the same day. The released code (github.com/Kris-camp/loft) defaults to a 5-term Cayley–Neumann transform with R^T R = (I - X^6)^2, which is not exactly orthogonal; per the referee's inspection the gradient-based supports are not in the code release. Not in the Hugging Face PEFT tuners list at the pinned commit.
